notes.kkodi: Said at the door of a house before entering.

guidebook.intro: The home: rooms, furniture and welcoming guests.

tips.title: Etogo, ekek
body: **Etogo** is a house or hut and **ekek** a door. **Ekicolong** is a chair. Many modern words are borrowed: **emeeza** (table), **etala** (lamp), **edirisa** (window).

tips.title: Kodi kodi! Kobuka!
body: At the door call **Kodi kodi!**; the host answers **Kobuka!** (come in). **Kiboi** is “sit”. Commands start with **ki-** or **ko-**.
**Alakara oni** means “we are happy”, a warm way to say a guest is welcome.

culture.title: The homestead
body: A traditional Iteso home, **ore**, is a ring of round huts around a yard, with a granary and a kraal for the cattle. Guests are offered a seat and something to drink before any business.
